identity.name: Phantom Taurus NET-STAR Cross-Plane Stitch — IIS Backdoor + Ntospy Credential Interception + SQL sa CSV Exfil Into One Incident
identity.summary: On one IIS host, XSIAM correlation stitches four orphan signals into a single credential-access incident: w3wp.exe runs the NET-STAR in-memory backdoor (EDR), an Ntospy network-provider DLL harvests logon credentials (identity), mssq.bat authenticates to SQL Server as 'sa' and exports CSVs (endpoint), and STAR-delimited AES/gzip data egresses over HTTPS from w3wp.exe (network).
identity.description: Phantom Taurus (CL-STA-0043 / TGR-STA-0043, Operation Diplomatic Specter) is a Chinese-nexus actor targeting foreign-affairs ministries, embassies, and telecoms across Africa, the Middle East, and Asia. Its NET-STAR suite is a fileless .NET toolset: the OutlookEN.aspx web-shell loader carries a Base64-compressed IIServerCore backdoor that runs inside the w3wp.exe IIS worker process, executing operator commands and loading arbitrary .NET assemblies in memory via AssemblyExecuter V1/V2 (which add AMSI + ETW bypass). This card is the CORRELATION-TERMINAL proof for the ANALYTICS plane: individually, each stage is a low-confidence orphan alert; together, on one IIS host inside a short window, they are an unmistakable credential-access intrusion. Stage 1 (EDR): w3wp.exe — a worker process that should never spawn cmd/powershell/wmic or compile assemblies — parents suspicious children (cmd/powershell/wmic), the observable signature of the in-memory backdoor — on-the-fly csc.exe/cvtres.exe ASP.NET compilation is deliberately excluded as benign IIS behavior. Stage 2 (identity): Ntospy registers a malicious network-provider DLL under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\NetworkProvider, intercepting credentials at the authentication-provider layer (T1556.008) — a NPPSpy-style network-provider abuse Unit 42 documents in its Operation Diplomatic Specter reporting. Stage 3 (endpoint): the harvested 'sa' credential is used by mssq.bat — deployed via WMI Win32_Process.Create (T1047) — to run sqlcmd against SQL Server, filter rows on diplomatic/geographic keywords, and export CSVs (T1005). Stage 4 (network): the collected data is STAR-delimited, AES-ECB/PKCS7 encrypted, gzip-compressed, Base64-encoded, and POSTed over HTTPS directly from w3wp.exe (T1071.001). A supporting timestomp BIOC catches the backdoor's changeLastModified command rewriting ASPX file times (T1070.006). The deployable content is four BIOCs (one per stage plus timestomp), two validation/hunt XQL queries, and one correlation rule (CR-MP-0017) that fuses the stages on a single agent_hostname into one Phantom Taurus credential-access incident anchored to the w3wp.exe causality chain — the F2 cross-plane-stitch demo where XSIAM turns three-to-four orphan alerts into one incident no single-plane tool assembles. Three real NET-STAR DLL SHA256 IOCs from the Unit 42 report ground the card.

campaigns: Operation Diplomatic Specter — espionage against foreign-affairs ministries, embassies, and telecoms (2023-2026)

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-MP-011 — Phantom Taurus NET-STAR cross-plane credential-access stitch (IIS backdoor + Ntospy + SQL sa exfil), correlation-terminal on the ANALYTICS plane.

prerequisites.description: Cortex XDR / XSIAM agent installed on the IIS host so per-process, registry, file, and network telemetry reaches xdr_data.
EDR, ITDR/identity, and NDR telemetry are all ingested into the same XSIAM tenant so the correlation engine can stitch the stages on one agent_hostname.

payload.code:
# SAFE-MODE emulation of the Phantom Taurus NET-STAR cross-plane chain.
# The real technique is Windows-native (w3wp.exe + WMI + SQL Server); the
# pov-engine emulates the cross-plane SIGNAL SHAPE non-destructively with marker
# files and no network egress, so the correlation logic can be exercised safely.
set -euo pipefail
WORK="${WORK_DIR:-/tmp/cortexsim-mp011}"
mkdir -p "$WORK"
echo '[MP-011] EDR: w3wp.exe -> IIServerCore in-memory backdoor child (cmd.exe/powershell.exe) [SAFE-MODE marker]' | tee "$WORK/step01-iis-backdoor.marker"
echo '[MP-011] identity: Ntospy network-provider DLL registered under HKLM\CurrentControlSet\Control\NetworkProvider [SAFE-MODE marker]' | tee "$WORK/step02-ntospy.marker"
echo '[MP-011] endpoint: mssq.bat via WMI Win32_Process.Create -> sqlcmd -U sa -o export.csv [SAFE-MODE marker, no SQL]' | tee "$WORK/step03-sql-sa-csv.marker"
printf 'AFGHANISTANSTARPAKISTANSTAR' | base64 > "$WORK/step04-star-exfil.b64"
echo '[MP-011] network: STAR-delimited AES/gzip base64 payload staged for HTTPS POST from w3wp [SAFE-MODE, no egress]'
echo '[MP-011] ANALYTICS: CR-MP-0017 stitches EDR+identity+NDR into one Phantom Taurus credential-access incident'

input_variables.name: WORK_DIR
input_variables.description: Scratch directory the SAFE-MODE markers are written to and removed from at cleanup.

expected_artifacts.description: w3wp.exe parenting an anomalous child process (cmd.exe/powershell.exe/pwsh.exe/wmic.exe) — the IIServerCore in-memory backdoor executing operator commands.
A network-provider registration/write under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\NetworkProvider referencing an attacker DLL (Ntospy credential interception).
WmiPrvSE.exe spawning cmd/sqlcmd running mssq.bat with an 'sa' login and CSV output.
Outbound HTTPS (tcp/443) initiated by w3wp.exe carrying STAR-delimited Base64 (AES/gzip) POST bodies.

iocs.context: NET-STAR IIServerCore backdoor (ServerCore.dll) loaded in-memory inside w3wp.exe. Unit 42 Phantom Taurus report.
NET-STAR AssemblyExecuter V1 (ExecuteAssembly.dll) — loads arbitrary .NET assemblies in memory. Unit 42 Phantom Taurus report.
NET-STAR AssemblyExecuter V2 (ExecuteAssembly.dll) — adds AMSI + ETW bypass. Unit 42 Phantom Taurus report.

biocs.name: MP-011 w3wp IIS Worker In-Memory Backdoor Child Process
biocs.description: The IIS worker process w3wp.exe parents a command interpreter or WMI — the observable signature of the NET-STAR IIServerCore in-memory backdoor executing operator commands and AssemblyExecuter loading assemblies in memory. A healthy w3wp.exe serves requests; it does not spawn cmd/powershell/wmic. Compiler children (csc.exe/cvtres.exe) are deliberately excluded because classic ASP.NET/IIS hosts spawn them for legitimate runtime .aspx page compilation, so they are not a reliable anomaly.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name = "w3wp.exe" or actor_process_image_name = "w3wp.exe"
| filter action_process_image_name in ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "wmic.exe")
| comp count() as backdoor_children by agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_image_name, actor_process_instance_id
| filter backdoor_children >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_image_name, actor_process_instance_id, backdoor_children

biocs.name: MP-011 Ntospy Network Provider DLL Credential Interception
biocs.description: Ntospy installs a malicious network-provider DLL by writing under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\NetworkProvider, intercepting plaintext credentials at the authentication-provider layer as users and services log on. Ntospy's NPPSpy-style network-provider registration is documented in Unit 42's Operation Diplomatic Specter report; the NetworkProvider/ProviderOrder registration mechanism is defined by MITRE T1556.008. Legitimate network providers are rare and installed by trusted installers, not by web-server or scripting processes.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.REGISTRY
| filter action_registry_key_name contains "CurrentControlSet\\Control\\NetworkProvider"
| filter action_registry_value_name = "ProviderOrder" or action_registry_data contains ".dll"
| comp count() as provider_writes by agent_hostname, actor_process_image_name
| filter provider_writes >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, actor_process_image_name, provider_writes

biocs.name: MP-011 WMI-Spawned SQL sa CSV Export via mssq bat
biocs.description: mssq.bat is deployed via WMI Win32_Process.Create and runs sqlcmd against SQL Server using the 'sa' system-administrator login, filtering rows on diplomatic/geographic keywords and exporting matches to CSV. Detect WmiPrvSE.exe parenting cmd/sqlcmd with an 'sa' login and file output — the NET-STAR database-direct exfil stage.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter actor_process_image_name = "WmiPrvSE.exe"
| filter action_process_image_name in ("cmd.exe", "sqlcmd.exe")
| filter action_process_command_line contains "mssq" or action_process_command_line contains "-U sa" or action_process_command_line contains ".csv"
| comp count() as sql_exports by agent_hostname, actor_process_image_name
| filter sql_exports >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, actor_process_image_name, sql_exports

biocs.name: MP-011 IIS Webroot ASPX Timestomp via changeLastModified
biocs.description: The IIServerCore changeLastModified command timestomps the OutlookEN.aspx web-shell loader to match a legitimate ASPX file, hiding the implant from modified-time triage. Detect a file-time modification on a .aspx file under the IIS webroot performed by the w3wp.exe worker process itself.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE and event_sub_type = ENUM.FILE_TIMES_MODIFIED
| filter actor_process_image_name = "w3wp.exe"
| filter action_file_path contains "inetpub" and action_file_extension = "aspx"
| filter action_file_modification_time < action_file_creation_time or action_file_modification_time > current_time()
| comp count() as timestomp_events by agent_hostname, action_file_path
| filter timestomp_events >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, action_file_path, timestomp_events

xql_queries.name: MP-011 Anomalous w3wp Child Process Surfaced on IIS Host
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900)
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name = "w3wp.exe" or actor_process_image_name = "w3wp.exe"
| filter action_process_image_name in ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "wmic.exe")
| comp count() as child_procs by agent_hostname, actor_process_instance_id
| filter child_procs >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, actor_process_instance_id, child_procs

xql_queries.name: MP-011 STAR-Delimited Encrypted HTTPS Exfil from w3wp
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900)
| filter event_type = ENUM.NETWORK
| filter actor_process_image_name = "w3wp.exe"
| filter action_remote_port = 443
| comp count() as egress_sessions, sum(action_total_upload) as bytes_out by agent_hostname, action_remote_ip
| filter egress_sessions >= 1
| sort desc bytes_out
| fields agent_hostname, action_remote_ip, egress_sessions, bytes_out

correlation_rules.name: Phantom Taurus NET-STAR Credential-Access Incident — Cross-Plane Stitch
correlation_rules.logic: BIOC(MP-011 w3wp IIS Worker In-Memory Backdoor Child Process) AND BIOC(MP-011 Ntospy Network Provider DLL Credential Interception) AND (BIOC(MP-011 WMI-Spawned SQL sa CSV Export via mssq bat) OR XQL(MP-011 STAR-Delimited Encrypted HTTPS Exfil from w3wp)) within 900s on the same agent_hostname — fuses the IIS in-memory backdoor execution (EDR), the network-provider credential interception (identity/ITDR), the SQL sa CSV export (endpoint), and the STAR-delimited AES/gzip HTTPS egress (NDR) into one Phantom Taurus credential-access incident anchored to the w3wp.exe causality chain on a single IIS host. The stitch is the declared causality spine: the credential-theft and credential-reuse stages join on the shared host entity (shared_entity, stitching_key = src_host / agent_hostname), and the w3wp endpoint process is joined to its outbound HTTPS exfil session (endpoint_network_stitch); every stage resolves to the same causality_actor_process = w3wp.exe (the CGO).

threat_scenarios.name: Cross-Plane Credential-Access Incident Stitching — Phantom Taurus NET-STAR
threat_scenarios.description: Prove that XSIAM's correlation engine assembles the four low-confidence, single-plane NET-STAR signals on one IIS host — in-memory backdoor (EDR), Ntospy credential interception (identity), SQL 'sa' CSV export (endpoint), and STAR-delimited HTTPS exfil (NDR) — into one credential-access incident that no single-plane tool reconstructs, and measure the cross-source correlation rate.

threat_steps.objective: The four NET-STAR stage signals from one IIS host stitch into a single incident_id spanning EDR + identity + NDR within the correlation window.
preconditions: IIS host with the Cortex XDR/XSIAM agent installed.
EDR, ITDR/identity, and NDR telemetry ingested into one XSIAM tenant.
steps: Emulate the w3wp in-memory backdoor child, Ntospy provider write, WMI SQL 'sa' export, and STAR-delimited HTTPS egress on one host.
Confirm CR-MP-0017 raises exactly one stitched credential-access incident.
success_criteria: BIOC `MP-011 w3wp IIS Worker In-Memory Backdoor Child Process` fires.
BIOC `MP-011 Ntospy Network Provider DLL Credential Interception` fires.
Correlation `CR-MP-0017` raises exactly one incident whose causality chain spans EDR + identity + NDR on one agent_hostname.

threat_steps.objective: Each stage stands alone as an evidenced detection so the DC can show the pre-correlation orphan alerts.
preconditions: Same host and tenant as TS-MP-011A.
steps: Run the WMI SQL 'sa' export stage.
success_criteria: BIOC `MP-011 WMI-Spawned SQL sa CSV Export via mssq bat` fires on the WMI/sqlcmd lineage.
BIOC `MP-011 IIS Webroot ASPX Timestomp via changeLastModified` fires on the file-time modification.

threat_steps.objective: The NET-STAR DLL SHA256 IOCs match on file/module telemetry when the samples are present.
preconditions: Cortex XDR agent hashing loaded modules on the IIS host.
steps: Ensure module-hash telemetry reaches the tenant.
Confirm the three ServerCore/ExecuteAssembly SHA256 IOCs are matchable.
success_criteria: At least one NET-STAR DLL SHA256 IOC matches a loaded/observed module when the sample is present.

preventive_controls: Constrain the IIS application-pool identity: deny it the ability to spawn cmd/powershell/wmic and to write the IIS webroot (AppLocker / WDAC + least-privilege app-pool account) so an in-memory backdoor cannot execute operator commands.
Monitor and lock down HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\NetworkProvider registration so a malicious network-provider DLL (Ntospy) cannot be installed to intercept credentials.
Retire or vault the SQL Server 'sa' account, enforce least-privilege service logins, and disable WMI process creation from web-server hosts where it is not required.
detection_engineering: Alert on w3wp.exe parenting a command interpreter or WMI (cmd/powershell/pwsh/wmic) — a worker process should never do this; exclude csc.exe/cvtres.exe, which are benign ASP.NET runtime compilation.
Alert on network-provider registry writes and on WmiPrvSE.exe spawning sqlcmd with an 'sa' login and CSV output.
Stitch the per-plane signals on agent_hostname into one incident (CR-MP-0017) rather than triaging four orphan alerts separately; measure the cross-source correlation rate as the KPI.
